question: What was the performance of multilingual BERT?

answer.free_form_answer: BERT had 76.6 F1 macro score on x-stance dataset.
evidence: To put the supervised score into context we list scores that variants of Bert have achieved on other stance detection datasets in Table TABREF46. It seems that the supervised part of x-stance has a similar difficulty as the SemEval-2016 BIBREF0 or MPCHI BIBREF22 datasets on which Bert has previously been evaluated.

title: X-Stance: A Multilingual Multi-Target Dataset for Stance Detection
answer_short: M-Bert performs consistently better than majority class baselines, shows zero-shot transfer capability, and generalizes cross-lingually and cross-target, though with a performance gap.
answer_rationale: The retrieved documents indicate that Multilingual BERT (M-Bert) outperforms majority class baselines in both cross-lingual and cross-target settings, demonstrates zero-shot transfer capability, and generalizes to unseen languages and targets, albeit with a performance gap compared to supervised settings. This is supported by results in Tables TABREF36 and TABREF37, as well as conclusions in Text 6 and 7.
